newsitem.title: UK: Details of UK Labour pledge on telephone companies.
newsitem.headline: Details of UK Labour pledge on telephone companies.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party said in its business manifesto published on Friday that it planned gradually to lift restrictions on the freedom of phone companies to offer entertainment services from 1998.
The following is the relevant section of the manifesto: "In telecommunications, all aspects of the industry are becoming increasingly competitive.
"We will encourage competition for the benefit of business and consumers through lower prices, improved quality and greater innovation.
"We seek rapid development across the country of the high-grade networks necessary for interactive communications.

"So we propose, from 1998, to progressively lift the present restrictions on the ability of telephone companies, such as BT and Cable and Wireless, to offer entertainment services over their networks.

"Our objective is full competition throughout the country. In turn we will expect the telecoms companies to make broader-band communications links available, as far as practicable, throughout the country. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5425528
